newsitem.title: USA: CNA, Capsure amend merger terms.
newsitem.headline: CNA, Capsure amend merger terms.

text.p: CNA Financial Corp and Capsure Holdings Corp said they have amended certain terms of their definitive merger agreement to form CNA Surety Corp.

In a release dated July 14, the companies said the changes include a cash dividend to be paid to Capsure stockholders, changes to the terms of a reinsurance agreement and a post-closing exchange ratio adjustment mechanism.
After the transaction closed, they said CNA Surety would pay a cash dividend to Capsure holders as of the closing date.
The dividend is estimated at $0.57 a share or $9.0 million based on a mid-September completion but would be figured according to the actual closing date.

The exchange ratio would be adjusted on March 31, 1998, if the net written premiums of the combined businesses were different from specified levels. Adjustments would be made through the surrender or issuance of shares by or to CNA.
As of the closing date, CNA's stockholdings in CNA Surety would be 61.75 percent. If an adjustment were made, CNA's ownership could range from 53.87 percent to 63.53 percent.

The adjustment mechanism is in response to an unexpected decline in first quarter premium volume of CNA Surety operations. The companies said CNA's surety premiums would be subject to quarterly fluctuations because the company would focuses on larger contract accounts. Second quarter 1997 CNA surety premiums were close to targeted levels, they said.
Completion of the merger is subject to Capsure stockholder approval as well as insurance regulatory approval.
In December, CNA and Capsure signed an agreement to form the largest U.S. surety firm.
